These were frozen literal text in v1 because HONORIFIC/PRONOUN_SUBJ/PATIENT_NOUN_MARKED are unscored fields with no span to recover from -- see module note.

v2 fix: 'De {AGE_ADJ} patiente werd gezien' (passive, leading article+marked-noun+gendered-participle) restructured to 'Nous avons revu {NAME_PATIENT}, {PATIENT_NOUN_MARKED} de {AGE_ADJ}, en consultation...' (active voice, object after verb) -- avoids both the Le/La-must-agree-with-a-slot problem and the avoir+participle agreement trap (French past participles with avoir only agree with a FRONTED direct object; putting the object after the verb sidesteps the whole issue), same fix pattern already used in pii_table_fr.py's own DEMO_TEMPLATE.

v2 fix: 'ivm Ibuprofen 400 mg' incorrectly rendered as 'ATCD Ibuprofen' in v1 (meaning drift -- ivm means 'in relation to', not 'history of') -- corrected to 'en lien avec Ibuprofen 400 mg', matching the abbreviation policy already used correctly elsewhere in this same template.

RAS (Dutch 'ras'=race/ethnicity, false friend vs. the real French abbreviation RAS) -> ORIGINE; code-switch fragments 'shared decision making'/'wall thickening' kept in English; distractor terms cross-matched to pii_table_fr.py's DISTRACTORS; {RELATIVE_RELATION} slot used in place of hardcoded 'Tante' (same fix as v1, retained).

v2 fix: 'Status' section ('{AGE_ADJ}, patient in stabiele algemene toestand... Bewust, georienteerd, mobiel') hardcoded masculine-default adjective agreement in v1 ('Conscient, oriente' with no feminine option) -- now uses {PATIENT_NOUN_MARKED} for the noun and '(e)' bracketed alternate endings for the two adjectives that must agree with the patient's sex (Conscient(e), oriente(e)) since there is no slot mechanism for adjective agreement; flagging this bracketed-alternate approach for review as a stopgap, not a first-choice pattern -- worth deciding a standard convention for adjective agreement before scaling to 50 templates.

v2 fix: 'hij werdt gestart' -> {PRONOUN_SUBJ} + 'a ete mis(e)' (bracketed alternate again, past-participle-with-etre-style agreement -- 'mis' is invariant with avoir+object-follows, actually reconsider: 'mis sous' takes avoir not etre, so agreement isn't triggered by subject -- kept the (e) as an extra-safe belt-and-braces marker pending confirmation this is even necessary).

TURP -> RTUP (real French urology initialism, not a distractor-pool item); M. Supraspinatus -> 'm. sus-epineux'; 'molaire zwangerschap uitgesloten' (Mol homograph) -> 'examen du mons pubis sans particularite' (Mons homograph) both occurrences.

v2 fix (reviewer's suggestion, agreed with): 'Pieter zegt dat hij...' -- a bare leaked first name, unlabeled, in the ORIGINAL Dutch corpus -- v1 substituted another bare name ('Marc'), which the reviewer correctly pointed out doesn't remove the unlabeled-name-shaped-span risk for NER training. v2 drops the bare name entirely and uses {PRONOUN_SUBJ} instead ('il/elle ajoute que...'), which both removes the risky unlabeled name-shaped token and fixes the underlying hardcoded-hij problem in the same stroke.
v2 fix: 'hij meldt' -> {PRONOUN_SUBJ}; hardcoded 'patient' in header and Besluit -> {PATIENT_NOUN_GENERIC}/{PATIENT_NOUN_MARKED} with the same active-voice restructuring as the other 4 templates.

'beers-teken afwezig' (Beers homograph) dropped rather than force-substituted -- already 3 other homographs used across this 5-template pilot batch (Marche, Mons, Ath); didn't want to cram a weak 4th into an already-dense sentence.

M. Subscapularis -> 'm. sous-scapulaire' (real French anatomical term, not a pii_table_fr.py distractor-pool item); ASCII table cell contents translated (ABI -> IPS, matching real French vascular-medicine usage, since French uses 'Indice de Pression Systolique' not the English initialism).
